items.text: Oil and gas have retreated modestly (WTI -2.1%, Brent -2.2%) but remain elevated at $84–92/bbl, keeping underlying cost-push risks alive. Sentiment gains in late July were captured before the July 7 escalation in Iran strikes, which has already begun re-inflaming prices; this represents a key tail risk to both consumer sentiment and CPI trajectories through 2H.

June payrolls printed a disappointing 57K vs. 129K prior, paired with unemployment rising to 4.2%, signaling a material softening in the labor market. Initial claims at 197K (up from 188K) add to the cautious tone. For a special-situations investor, this raises refinancing risk for leveraged names exposed to recession and improves the credit-negative backdrop for consumer-dependent sectors.

CPI and PPI have both rolled over (CPI headline 3.46%, core 2.57%; PPI 5.51%), and the curve flattened sharply to 47bp ahead of late July geopolitical shocks. While rear-view data looks encouraging, the oil spike and currency effects could re-arrest disinflation. Core PCE remains sticky above 3.0% and 1-yr UMich expectations sit at 4.2%—sticky anchors for rates and credit spreads.

Fed funds unchanged at 3.75% through July; ECB held at 2.25% deposit rate on July 23. Both central banks remain data-dependent with inflation concerns tempered by labor softening. Market is pricing modest rate-cut risk in 2H 2026 if growth continues to cool, a positive tail for floating-rate credit but pressure on covenant flexibility in stressed names.

HY OAS at 284bp (up 3bp) and IG at 80bp (down 1bp) remain historically tight despite labor weakness and growth deceleration, suggesting credit complacency. CCC OAS widening to 1006bp signals emerging stress at the lower end. For special situations, this dispersion is the opportunity set—sector-specific and idiosyncratic dislocations are more valuable than broad-based macro hedges.

Atlanta Fed's GDPNow jumped to 4.95% (from 1.54%) ahead of preliminary May/June data, but Q2 actual GDP came in soft at 1.5% YoY. ISM Manufacturing PMI at 53.3 in June (slowing from 54.0), ISM Services at 54.0 in June. China's manufacturing PMI fell to contraction (49.2 in July) for the first time since March, signaling global growth deceleration risks.

UMich sentiment rebounded sharply to preliminary 54.4 (final 55.2) in July—led by easing gas prices—but remains 11% below year-ago levels and sits near 2nd percentile historically. Housing starts accelerated to 1,427K but existing home sales slipped to 4.09M. Savings rate at 2.7% signals stretched households; retail sales YoY cooling to 6.95% hints at demand exhaustion if income doesn't hold.

themeCards.title: Oil/Geopolitical Shock Resurge
themeCards.statusLine: July 7 resumption of US–Iran strikes has re-inflamed energy prices and sentiment risks after brief July pullback. Survey data (UMich, PMI) was collected before escalation, so downside surprises possible in August prints.
themeCards.relevance: Direct pressure on inflation expectations (1-yr at 4.2%, sticky), consumer spending power, and energy/transport-exposed credit. Refinancing risk peaks if growth data disappoints and inflation re-accelerates.

themeCards.title: Global Growth Deceleration — China Contraction Signal
themeCards.statusLine: China manufacturing PMI fell below 50 (49.2) in July after brief June rebound, ending 4-month growth streak. Non-manufacturing also slipped. Signals weakening global demand and potential re-escalation of US–China trade tension.
themeCards.relevance: Pressures commodity/EM credit, increases refinancing risk for export-dependent sectors, and could force more fiscal stimulus globally. Extends duration of low-growth regime, narrowing equity multiples and tightening credit pick-up in credit markets.

themeCards.title: US Labor Market Deterioration
themeCards.statusLine: June nonfarm payrolls disappointed sharply at 57K vs. 129K prior; unemployment rose to 4.2%. Initial claims edged up to 197K. Labor income growth (AHE +3.52%) barely outpacing inflation, stretching household leverage.
themeCards.relevance: Erodes debt service capacity for consumer-levered credits (auto, BNPL, credit card securitization). Increases recession tail risk and triggers covenant-cushion compression in cyclical leverage, creating refinancing urgency for 2026–27 maturities.

themeCards.title: Credit Spread Compression & Dispersion Opportunity
themeCards.statusLine: HY OAS tight at 284bp, IG at 80bp, but CCC OAS widening to 1006bp signals emerging stress at lower quality. Broad indices mask widening divergence between upper-tranche and distressed.
themeCards.relevance: Creates asymmetric special-situations optionality: tighter upper brackets compress risk-adjusted carry, forcing capital into idiosyncratic dislocations and distressed turnarounds. Favorable for selective CCC long/short positioning and restructuring plays.

themeCards.title: Sticky Core Inflation & Curve Re-Flattening Risk
themeCards.statusLine: Core inflation (2.57% CPI, 3.29% PCE) remains sticky; curve compressed to 47bp on July 31. Energy shocks and potential Fed hawkishness could re-invert curve, testing credit timing assumptions and duration hedging.
themeCards.relevance: Compressed curve and sticky core constrain Fed's ability to deliver deep rate cuts, keeping floating-rate debt serviceable but extending duration of high real rates. Tests assumptions on 2H26 refinancing windows and covenant breach probability for marginally-levered names.

themeCards.title: Housing & Consumer Durables Demand Softness
themeCards.statusLine: Existing home sales declining (4.09M vs 4.19M), mortgage rates up to 6.66%, 30-yr ARM resets continuing to pressure affordability. Retail sales ex-autos slowing YoY (6.95% from 7.92%), savings rate at 2.7% lowest in cycle.
themeCards.relevance: CRE refinancing wall extends into 2027 as cap-rate compression stalls. Housing finance and manufactured-housing ABS face prepayment risk if rates stay high. Consumer goods credit (auto loans, BNPL) faces rising default risk if income doesn't re-accelerate.

chinaPMI.delta: down 1.1 from June 50.3, now in contraction

ismServices.delta: down 0.5 from May 54.5; July data releases August 5

consensus.CPI: 3.0–3.2% YoY expected for July (headline); Core PCE ~3.0% YoY expected
consensus.PPI: ~4.5–4.8% YoY expected for July (headline); core ~3.5% YoY
consensus.GDP: No new release; Q2 actual was 1.5% YoY; GDPNow at 4.95% for 2026 annualized

regime.label: Stagnation Risk Emerging
regime.detail: Labor deteriorating, growth decelerating globally, sticky core inflation, energy tail risk resurging, but credit spreads compressed—late-cycle distribution with asymmetric downside.
